notes:
The sheet continues the description of connected oriented contours by a cyclic order n and a torsor, then lists data for a connected contour and replaces its second datum by a two-element Ω mapping to inverse generators. Two lower summaries concern contours not assumed connected; the second ends in an ellipsis-like trace, with un retained as an alternative. There is no title or manuscript date. Archive pencil foliation 6 is comment-only. The inserted tel, smaller interlinear parenthesis, three cancellations, two bullet marks and short rising separator are preserved. The opening parenthesis before savoir remains unclosed. G⁰ becomes bare G in 2 bis; no superscript is supplied.

The main reading of the map is r|σ. The second base in the displayed pair has a short s-like shape unlike the preceding descending g: retain s|g, despite the attractive inverse-pair formula. The three readers' local check (M007-I) that an order-n generator has a two-element inverse pair precisely when n≠2 applies only to the g alternative. The small shorthand remains sss|ss|ssi; that algebra does not decide its letters. M007-W2 checks that two distinct elements of Ω can have the same image when n=2. The author's qualifications Du moins si n≥3 and pas néc. / pas néc are kept; the opening bound is 2, not a written question mark.

Main construction check M007-C builds the degree-two graph from the finite cyclic torsor and the two-element Ω, preserving the parallel edges at n=2. It is not an unqualified equivalence proof. The formulation with ordinary n∈ℕ misses the two-sided infinite contour (M007-F); the infinite cyclic torsor supplies that component (M007-FINF). Interpreting the lower acted-on set as vertices, an arbitrary ℤ-action also allows a fixed point, incompatible with the earlier two-distinct-endpoints axiom (M007-Z). The fixed-point-free successor-permutation construction is checked as M007-ZNF. Its directed-edge notion of orientation is not identified without qualification with scan006's automorphism-based definition, especially at two vertices. These limitations affect only the notes; the written assertions remain unchanged.

events.who: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort inherited/not exposed; scan007 main
events.outcome: For the finite cyclic data with n>=2, a torsor S and a two-element set Omega={a,b} mapping to inverse generators g and g inverse, construct edges as the orbits of tau(s,a)=(g.s,b), tau(s,b)=(g inverse.s,a) on S x Omega. Tau is an involution without fixed points because it switches a and b. Each edge joins two distinct vertices since g is nonidentity; each vertex has two distinct incident edges. Generation by g gives connectedness. For n>=3 this is the ordinary n-cycle; for n=2 the two edge orbits are parallel edges between the two vertices. The separate two-element Omega therefore retains the doubled-edge data which the singleton inverse pair loses. This is a construction check, not an unqualified categorical equivalence proof and not a resolution of any handwritten symbol.

Refined statement M007-FINF: the finite description applies to finite components; include the infinite cyclic group Z for the two-sided infinite component. All three complete readings have n in N, and the main bound crop confirms n>=2. No infinity symbol is supplied from this check.

Thus the infinite cyclic case repairs the specific omitted infinite component in M007-F.

The components are cycles of length at least two or two-sided infinite paths. Conversely a directed contour with one incoming and one outgoing edge per vertex gives this fixed-point-free successor permutation.
